title: Toad in the Hole
subtitle: British sausages baked in Yorkshire pudding batter
excerpt: The great British baked supper: fat pork sausages browned in a screaming-hot roasting tin and then enveloped in Yorkshire pudding batter that puffs up dramatically around them, emerging golden and slightly crisp at the edges and wonderfully soft within. Served with onion gravy.

recipe.sourceNotes: Toad in the hole is a British baked dish combining sausages and Yorkshire pudding batter, with clear origins in eighteenth century British cooking. The name is believed to derive from the resemblance of the sausages peering out of the risen batter to frogs or toads peering out of rock crevices. The dish is essentially a Yorkshire pudding (a batter of eggs, flour, and milk, baked in a very hot pan with fat) with sausages baked into it. The key technique is the same as for Yorkshire pudding: the fat in the tin must be smoking hot before the cold batter is poured in, which creates the immediate steam and rise. Resting the batter for at least 30 minutes (or overnight) allows the gluten to relax and the batter to become more fluid, which produces a better, more even rise.

content.text: The hot fat is critical: if the tin is not smoking hot and the fat is not visibly shimmering when the batter goes in, the pudding will not rise. Make the batter at least 30 minutes in advance. Do not open the oven door for the first 20 minutes of cooking. Serve immediately; the pudding will begin to deflate within minutes of coming out of the oven.
Make the batter: whisk the flour, eggs, and milk together until completely smooth. Season with salt. Leave to rest for at least 30 minutes.

Heat the oven to 220°C / fan 200°C / gas 7. Add the oil to a large roasting tin (about 30 x 20 cm). Place in the oven for 5 minutes until the oil is smoking. Add the sausages and cook for 15 minutes until browned.

Working quickly, pour the batter around the sausages in one go. Return immediately to the oven. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the batter is risen, golden, and set. Do not open the door during baking. Serve at once with onion gravy.
